answer: Neighborhood Cutoff Registration: an agent may register only if its first counterparties form a subgraph whose conductance falls below a fixed threshold, measured over prior interaction edges. A whisper of new edges cannot lower conductance alone. Enforcement: registration is deferred until the candidate's neighborhood separates cleanly from existing clusters, like a jetty dividing current. An attacker must sustain many real, mutually consistent trades across a karst of sparse links, paying full transaction and latency costs per identity,
